title: Thou Seest My Feebleness
description: Thou Seest My Feebleness in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Charles Wesley wrote these words. They were printed in the supplement of the 1866 edition of A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1866), as hymn 516, “For Help in Temptation”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thou seest my fee-ble-ness; Fa-ther! be Thou my power, My help and re-fuge in dis-tress, My for-tress and my tower!

lines: My help and refuge in distress,
Give me to trust in Thee;
My helm and sword and buckler be,
But strength in Thee I surely have,
Thou lovest me, Father, as Thine own,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1866); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
